Produced by tools/mobile/wire-probe.mjs. This file exists because the mobile
audit's single largest transferable number (doc 91 §G4: 'script bytes 4,247 KB
against a 1,200 KB budget') was measured on a `next dev` Turbopack build and
quoted against a budget field whose own doc comment says 'of which JS, GZIPPED,
KB'. It compared a raw dev byte to a compressed production budget. The rows
below are the same route, the same device, the same cold cache and the same
reader, on both builds, so the dev→prod ratio is a measurement rather than an
TO REPRODUCE (both servers need their own port and their own KNIJKA_DIST_DIR):
prod: KNIJKA_DIST_DIR=.next-<lane> npx next build && npx next start --port P
…behind TLS — see `productionNeedsTls` below, it is not optional.
dev:  KNIJKA_DIST_DIR=.next-<lane> npx next dev --port Q
loadState: cold HTTP cache, warm session (signed in in a throwaway context, storageState reused)

tier.readFrom: [sim-perf] tier=low facadeMaps=colorOnly clearcoat=false maxDpr=1 shadows=false postprocessing=false
tier.why: seedQualityFromSignals rule 3 — touch-only and dpr 3 ≥ 2. This IS the tier a phone runs at, so these are phone numbers, not desktop numbers.

productionNeedsTls.fact: A production build served over plain http://localhost loads ZERO JavaScript.
productionNeedsTls.mechanism: next.config.ts adds `upgrade-insecure-requests` to the ENFORCED CSP whenever NODE_ENV === 'production'. Under `next start` on http, every /_next/static/* subresource is rewritten to https:// and fails with SSL connect error; the login form then silently never submits.
productionNeedsTls.consequence: doc 91 §J Wave 0b ('Build production once (next build && next start) and repeat the perf sweep') cannot be followed literally. Put a TLS front in front of the server, or the sweep measures a page with no scripts on it.
productionNeedsTls.notABug: The header is correct in production, where the app is served over https. Only the localhost verification path needs the TLS front.

instrumentNotes: scriptBytesAsPerfProbeReadsIt = sum of transferSize where initiatorType === 'script' — the exact reading environment/PerfProbe.tsx used when §G4 was written, kept here for continuity.

jsTransferred = every .js the document pulled, however it was pulled. It is the honest parse budget: Next preloads chunks via <link rel=modulepreload> ('link'), and basis_transcoder.js / draco_wasm_wrapper.js arrive via fetch ('fetch'). PerfProbe missed 39.6 KB of real JS in production this way; that classifier has since been fixed.
wasm is reported separately and is NOT counted as script bytes — it is stream-compiled, not parsed as JS. It is inside firstPlayableWire.

resourceEntries is here because the resource-timing buffer holds 250 by default and then drops the rest silently. Dev is at 222 of 250. Anything at or over 250 makes every byte total on that row a FLOOR.

observedFps is CONTEXT ONLY. Bytes are a property of the build and transfer identically at 4 fps and at 60; no frame-time claim is made from this harness, and none may be attributed to the founder's handset.

rows.build: next dev (Turbopack) — the build every §G4 figure was taken on

productionIsViewportIndependent.claim: Bytes do not move with the viewport — measured, not assumed.
productionIsViewportIndependent.note: The URL SET is identical on all six — not one file differs. small-landscape is 13 KB heavier because it fetched /draco/draco_wasm_wrapper.js TWICE (139 entries vs 138, the only duplicate in any profile). Worth a look on its own: a second decoder fetch means something instantiated a second DRACOLoader rather than reusing the cached one.

productionJsByContent._: Every chunk /simulator pulls at tier low, attributed by fingerprinting the built file. gz = transferred, raw = decoded (what the JS engine parses). CHUNK NAMES ARE BUILD-SPECIFIC — Turbopack rehashes them on every build, so treat them as evidence of this run, not as handles to grep for later.

scenarioTemplateData.what: The whole scenario catalogue — ~150 ScenarioSpec templates with every level, rubric, mistake and Bulgarian instruction string. A session plays exactly one of them.
scenarioTemplateData.why: simulator-client.tsx calls scenarioById() synchronously inside a useMemo, and scenarioById is a lookup over SCENARIO_TEMPLATES, so the whole array is pulled into the client bundle. The catalogue's titles do NOT need it — page.tsx builds ScenarioCatalogEntry[] server-side and passes them as props.

composerSplitHoldsInProduction.claim: The doc 82 §2.3 composer code-split — the precedent for this whole line of work — is honoured by the production bundler, not just by the source.
composerSplitHoldsInProduction.evidence: The only built chunk containing SMAAEffect/BloomEffect/EffectAttribute is 2bz7z9pmqe7wg.js (385,879 B raw / 170,396 B gz). It does not appear in the /simulator resource timeline at tier low. __tests__/composerSplit.test.ts can only assert the source; this is the bundler agreeing.
composerSplitHoldsInProduction.worth: 170 KB gz / 386 KB raw of must-parse JS kept off a phone, every session.
